subject: Post-call: Technical evaluation milestones & acceptance criteria (MAP draft)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moore <alex.moore@priorytech.com>, Tanya Lopez <tanya.lopez@priorytech.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Technical evaluation milestones & acceptance criteria (MAP draft)

Thanks for the time today — great conversation. Per our call, I wanted to send a concise MAP draft for the technical evaluation milestone and capture the immediate next steps so we have a shared view going into the benchmark phase. I attached a spreadsheet (MAP_v1_PrioryTech.xlsx) and a lightweight benchmark template (benchmark_template.csv) to make data exchange easier.

Summary of the proposed Technical Evaluation milestone: 
- Objective: Validate model quality and production economics for PrioryTech's chat assistant use case (customer support triage + short-form summarization).
- Success criteria (acceptance):
  * Quality: end-to-end response accuracy/coverage >= 92% on the seeded evaluation set (per your sample prompts).
  * Latency: p95 single-request latency <= 220ms for 512-token context (target region: us-west).
  * Cost: average inference cost <= $1.80 per 1,000 user-facing tokens at expected concurrency profile (inc. batching).
  * Throughput: sustainable steady-state throughput >= 120 qps for mixed short/medium prompts with auto-batching.
- Model shortlist (initial): Llama 2 70B (quantized), Mistral-Instruct-32B, and an optimized Redwood-verified 34B variant.
- Deliverables: benchmark report (metrics vs. criteria), sample traces (p95 windows), a short recommendations memo (config & quantization).
- Owners and responsibilities:
  * PrioryTech technical lead: provide sample prompt set, representative payloads, and 2-week test account access to dev environment — due 2026-08-12 (Alex / Maya).
  * Redwood evaluation: run benchmarks, provide raw logs and summarized report — due 2026-08-28 (Ben / Jordan).
  * Integration check: validate inference integration and KV cache behavior w/ your staging data — due 2026-09-03 (Laura / PrioryTech infra).
- Dependencies and blockers:
  * Test account credentials & sample dataset (blocking until we receive it).
  * If sample size > 10k prompts we may need a small extension to the benchmark window; we flagged that in the attached template.

Proposed target close date for the MAP milestone: 2026-09-30 (we can shorten if deliverables are accelerated).

Ask: Please confirm the owners and the feasibility of the acceptance criteria above. If any of the latency/cost targets look off on your side, call them out and we can adjust before we lock the dates.

Thanks — attaching MAP_v1 for edits.

—
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: MAP_v1_PrioryTech.xlsx (spreadsheet), benchmark_template.csv (csv)

From: Alex Moore <alex.moore@priorytech.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tanya Lopez <tanya.lopez@priorytech.com>
Date: 2026-08-06T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Technical evaluation milestones & acceptance criteria (MAP draft)

Thanks Ben — this is a useful first pass and aligns with our internal priorities. Quick notes from our side:

- Owners: I'll be primary for coordination (Alex Moore). I'm looped in with our CTO/MLE (Maya Singh) who will own the technical handoff for the sample dataset and staging access. I'll add Maya on the next message.
- Latency: p95 <= 220ms for 512 tokens seems ambitious but plausible; would you be able to give an estimate if we allow p95 <= 250ms for initial runs, then optimize to 220ms in a second pass?
- Cost: the $1.80 / 1k tokens target looks OK but we need to understand baseline with no batching (to see delta). Could Redwood provide both batched and unbatched cost estimates in the report?
- Throughput: 120 qps steady-state is our rough target; we will validate based on our expected concurrency (we'll share expected traffic curve).

Blocked items: We'll provide the seed prompt set and a small representative payload dump by 2026-08-12. Maya (maya.singh@priorytech.com) will follow up with infra contacts for test account setup.

One ask: can you include one short test that measures cold-start token latency for small requests (<= 64 tokens)? That helps our UX team.

Appreciate it — look forward to the benchmark template.

—
Alex Moore
Director, Product — PrioryTech
alex.moore@priorytech.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Moore <alex.moore@priorytech.com>
Date: 2026-08-07T11:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Technical evaluation milestones & acceptance criteria (MAP draft)

Looping in internally on the MAP itemization — quick internal notes and proposed owner assignments so we can update the customer: 

- Benchmarks & runbook: Jordan will be the primary for benchmark execution (Jordan Blake). He'll own test harness config and cost-run estimations.
- Reporting: I'll lead synthesis of the benchmark report and the recommendations memo; Ben will vet the performance tuning items.
- Model shortlist: suggest we replace "Redwood-verified 34B" label with a specific artifact name — "RW-34B-opt (int8)" — and add an alternate of Llama2-13B-chat if PrioryTech's production memory budget is tighter than expected.
- Acceptance criteria tweaks (proposed):
  * Latency: allow initial p95 <= 250ms for the first run (per Alex's note) and hard acceptance p95 <= 220ms by the second run (optimization window).
  * Cost: we'll report both batched and unbatched cost, and add a 95th-percentile cost bucket for worst-case estimate.
- Schedule adjustment: recommend we aim for a slightly earlier internal close so stakeholders can review before the end of quarter — propose moving target close to 2026-09-26, pending sample dataset on 8/12.

I'll create MAP_v1_PrioryTech_v2.xlsx with these adjustments and send back for Alex to review. Jordan, please call out any infra constraints if the throughput target requires dedicated concurrency testing.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Specials | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moore <alex.moore@priorytech.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@priorytech.com>

Date: 2026-08-11T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: MAP update: technical milestone acceptance criteria (v2)

Alex / Maya — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clarifications. Attached is MAP_v1_PrioryTech_v2.xlsx which incorporates Laura's proposed wording and the two-phase latency acceptance approach. Key updates below and immediate next steps: 

- Two-phase latency acceptance: Phase 1 (initial run): p95 <= 250ms; Phase 2 (optimization run): target p95 <= 220ms. Both runs will include cold-start checks for <=64-token requests per your UX ask.
- Cost reporting: we will include both batched and unbatched cost per 1k tokens and a 95th percentile worst-case snapshot.
- Model shortlist (finalized for first run): Llama2-70B (int8), Mistral-Instruct-32B, RW-34B-opt (int8). We will add Llama2-13B-chat as an alternate if memory budgets require it.
- Deliverable dates (updated):
  * PrioryTech provides sample dataset + infra access: due 2026-08-12 (Alex / Maya).
  * Redwood benchmark run complete + raw logs: due 2026-08-26 (Jordan).
  * Final report + recommendations: due 2026-09-20 (Laura / Ben).
  * Target MAP milestone close: 2026-09-26.

Next steps for Alex / Maya: confirm sample dataset delivery date and include any non-standard prompt routing or policy constraints (e.g., PII stripping rules) that need to be applied during the run. Once we have access, Jordan will schedule the first benchmark window (we'll share a calendar invite).

If that all looks good I'll mark the MAP milestone as "in progress" on the HubSpot deal and upload the v2 MAP doc to the shared Drive.

—
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
